classification.difficultyReason: Add the adjacent given angles and use their non-180-degree total to reject a straight-line claim.

content.prompt: Explain why PQR is not a straight line.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 7, below stem on the left
spec.description: Near-collinear QP and QR, with QS rising upper-right. P and R at the baseline endpoints, Q below the common vertex and S at the upper endpoint. Upper sectors carry 139° and 42°. No dots.
spec.mathematics: Candidate coordinates use QS at 42° to QR and QP at 181° to QR, preserving the stated adjacent angles. The resulting 1° baseline departure requires source review because it is not measurable reliably from the raster.
spec.answerVisibility: Only P, Q, R, S and the supplied 139° and 42° labels are visible.

answer.short: $139°+42°=181°$, which is not $180°$, so PQR is not a straight line.
answer.worked:
$$139°+42°=181°$$
Angles on a straight line add up to $180°$. The adjacent angles at Q total $181°$, so PQR is not a straight line.
